extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and parties seeking judicial review of agency decisions; court clerks; D.C. Bar Board and D.C. Bar members
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules for initiating and litigating petitions for review of agency orders in the D.C. Court of Appeals (filing, service, timing, record filing, intervention, fees), together with proposed amendments and guiding principles for the D.C. Bar Rules and revised Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement of review — petition filing (original and copies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of an agency order or decision is commenced by filing with the Clerk an original and six copies of a petition for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interests make joinder practicable, two or more persons may join in a petition for review. Form 5 is a suggested form of a petition for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to file petition for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless an applicable statute provides a different time frame, the petition for review must be filed within 30 days after notice is given, in conformance with the rules or regulations of the agency, of the order or decision sought to be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the statute-prescribed time is less than 11 days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays are excluded in the computation unless the statute provides otherwise. If the order was made out of the presence of the parties and notice is by mail, the petitioner has 5 additional days from the date of mailing. A timely petition for rehearing/reconsideration in accordance with agency rules tolls the time to petition for review until notice of denial of rehearing is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition contents — naming parties and specifying order
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must: (A) name each party seeking review either in the caption or the body of the petition (using terms such as 'et al.,' 'petitioners,' or 'respondents' does not effectively name the parties); (B) name the agency as a respondent; and (C) specify the order or decision or part thereof to be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully identify each petitioner by name and precisely identify the challenged order or portion to avoid dismissal for insufficient specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases involving review of a decision of the Office of Administrative Hearings, the petition must name each party seeking review and specify the order or decision or part thereof; only the parties before the Office of Administrative Hearings and any other party permitted to participate by this court shall be parties in this court. The petition may not name either the Office of Administrative Hearings or the Administrative Law Judge from the Office of Administrative Hearings as a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow D.C. Code § 2-1831.16(h) and the separate procedural provisions governing OAH cases (see Rule 15(a)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by mail — receipt required for timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing may be accomplished by mail addressed to the Clerk, but filing will not be deemed timely unless the petition is, in fact, received by the Clerk within the prescribed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on mail, ensure actual receipt by the Clerk within the statutory/Rule deadline; do not assume mailing date equals filing date for timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for corporations and entities
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner is a corporation or other entity, the petition must be signed by counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition not bearing the necessary signature will be stricken unless omission of the signature is corrected promptly after being called to the attention of counsel or the party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-petition timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timely petition for review is filed by a party, any other party to the proceeding before the agency may file a cross-petition for review within 14 days after the petition was filed, or within 30 days of the date of the challenged order or decision, whichever period expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the later of the two periods carefully to determine cross-petition deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of the petition and filing of service list
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clerk must serve a copy of the petition for review on each respondent agency and on the Corporation Counsel (Office of the Attorney General) or other counsel representing any agency respondent. At the time of filing, the petitioner must serve (or have served) a copy on each party admitted to participate in the agency proceedings (except for agency respondents) and file with the Clerk a list of those so served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contemporaneous service on all required recipients and file the list of served parties to satisfy Rule 15(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention in agency cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to the agency proceeding who wants to intervene in this court must, within 30 days from the date the petition is filed, serve upon all parties and file with the Clerk a copy of a notice of intention to intervene, in which case the party will be deemed an intervenor without the necessity of filing a motion. Any other person who wants to intervene must file a motion to intervene with the Clerk within 30 days of the date on which the petition for review is filed, unless extended for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A motion to intervene must be served on all parties, contain a concise statement of the interest of the moving party and the grounds for intervention, and must state on which side the party seeks to intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees on filing petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing any separate or joint petition for review, the petitioner must pay the Clerk all required fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm applicable filing fees and submit payment with the petition to avoid processing/acceptance problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and expedited cases reference (Rule 25.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent applicable, Rule 25.1 (Emergency and Expedited Cases) governs review of certain agency orders or decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Rule 25.1 when the petition involves emergency or expedited relief to ensure compliance with its special procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency to file the record — timing and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent agency must file the record within 60 days after being served with a petition for review. In OAH cases, the Office of Administrative Hearings must file the record within 60 days of the issuance of an order directing the filing of the record. The court may shorten or extend these deadlines for good cause. The Clerk must notify all parties and intervenors that the record has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the 60-day deadline and be prepared to seek shortening/extension for good cause if necessary. Rely on the Clerk's notification for docketing of the record filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes filing of the record
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must file: (A) the original or a certified copy of the record on review or parts designated by the parties; or (B) if a partial record is filed, a certified list adequately describing all documents, transcripts, exhibits, and other material constituting the record on review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing a partial record, the certified list must adequately describe all material constituting the record on review so the court and parties can identify omitted materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulation that no record or certified list be filed
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties may stipulate in writing that no record or certified list be filed. The date when the stipulation is filed with the Clerk is treated as the date when the record is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written stipulation substitutes for filing the record but should be carefully drafted and promptly filed to fix the record-filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency retention of record portions not filed
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must retain any portion of the record not filed with the Clerk. All parts of the record retained by the agency are a part of the record on review for all purposes and, if the court or a party so requests, must be sent to the court regardless of any prior stipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retained materials remain part of the record and may be ordered produced; do not assume unstated items are beyond the court's review simply because not filed initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of time (Rule 26 interplay and Singer precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time computation for short periods has been governed by Rule 26(a)(2), which provides for excluding intervening Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays when calculating periods of less than 11 days; Rule 26(c) provides that calendar days should be used when adding five days if 'a party is required or permitted to act within a prescribed period after a paper is served on that party.' Singer v. Singer held that, in calculating the five-day period under the predecessor rule, intervening Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays do not count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to the interplay of Rule 26 provisions and case law (Singer) when computing deadlines; note the court is considering amending Rule 26(c) to clarify application to notices of appeal under Rules 4, 5, or 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Robert's Rules as parliamentary authority for Bylaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised is the desired and appropriate parliamentary authority for the Bar. Robert's Rules describes an organization's bylaws as the instrument that informs and 'defines the primary characteristics of the organization' and prescribes how the organization functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting bylaws, follow Robert's Rules conventions: bylaws should set fundamental organizational rules, require specified notice and vote for amendment, and not be subject to suspension or waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylaws drafting best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee recognized the following best practices when developing the revised Bylaws: bylaws can codify and memorialize established historical practices and procedures; when drafted properly, bylaws become 'evergreen' and require infrequent amendments; bylaws should be empowering and should not be unduly restrictive; bylaws should be readable and enforceable and provide flexibility without ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain, durable drafting that balances firmness (to preserve core rules) with flexibility for administration; move operational details to companion documents where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee goals for revised Bylaws and Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee adopted these principles and goals: create Bylaws that are an exemplar of good construction and adhere to best practices; develop an empowering and user-friendly document; remove administrative details from the Bylaws and migrate that content to other documents; define the roles and responsibilities of the Bar, the Board, committees, staff, and the membership; maintain and strengthen the fiscal integrity of the Bar; and provide governance guardrails and appropriate organizational flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these goals as touchstones when deciding what to place in Bylaws versus Rules or a Membership Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additions to Rule I purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed addition of two items to the Bar’s enumerated purposes in Rule I, Section 2: 'to assist the legal profession in maintaining high standards of the practice of law in the District of Columbia' and 'to promote access to justice and enhance the delivery of legal services to those in need.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These added purposes make the Rules align with the revised Bylaws and clarify the Bar's stated objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership: migrate periodic registration to Bylaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to delete Section 2 (Periodic Registration of Attorneys) from the Rules because Article III, Section 3.05 of the Bylaws sets forth members' requirements to file an annual registration statement with the Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational membership requirements belong in the Bylaws or Membership Manual rather than the Rules to avoid redundancy and allow more streamlined updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership: streamline mandatory course language
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation of editorial changes to Section 3 (Mandatory Course for New Admittees) to streamline and simplify the section; additional detail now appropriately resides in Article III, Section 3.05 of the Bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep core obligation language in the Rules and place procedural details (scheduling, administration) in the Bylaws or Membership Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership classes — add 'retired' class and Board authority for additional classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to clarify and update classes of D.C. Bar membership and to add a 'retired' class. The Rules would also authorize the Board to create additional classes of membership and establish the required qualifications for such classes, after consultation with the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow the Board limited authority (with Court consultation) to meet evolving membership needs while preserving Court oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology change: 'dues' to 'license fees'
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to change the title 'Membership Dues' to 'License Fees' and replace each instance of 'membership dues' or 'dues' with 'license fees' throughout the Rules. Rationale: 'dues' typically apply where membership is voluntary; 'license fees' better indicates a required payment to maintain a member's license and admission to the Court, supported by recent First Amendment jurisprudence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise terminology reflecting mandatory status of payments required to maintain license and admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove detailed penalty provisions from Rules (migrate to Bylaws)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to delete the section on 'Penalty for Nonpayment of Dues; Late Charges' from the Rules, because the substantive detail now resides in the Bylaws (e.g., 'Non-payment of license fees may result in suspension and the inability to practice law in the District of Columbia').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve core consequences in Bylaws; avoid duplicative, detailed penalty mechanics in the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation and reinstatement governance relocated
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to rename Section 8 'Resignation and Reinstatement' and provide that 'A member's resignation from and reinstatement into the Bar shall be governed by procedures prescribed by the Bar, which shall include consultation with the Office of Disciplinary Counsel.' These topics are fully addressed in the Membership Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegate procedural specifics to the Membership Manual while preserving the Rule-level principle that resignation/reinstatement procedures exist and involve ODC consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify Rules III–VI and migrate details to Bylaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that Rules III (Officers) through VI (Meetings of the Bar) retain only necessary, fundamental language, with the majority of board- and membership-meeting details migrated to the Bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep Rules succinct; use the Bylaws for composition, terms, duties, vacancies, meetings, voting, and Executive Committee details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain 'Public Expressions/Public Statements' language in Rule V
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to migrate almost all content of Rule V (Executive Committee) to the Bylaws except language regarding 'Public Expressions,' which should be retained as the sole content of Rule V renamed 'Public Statements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to legal challenges to unified bars, explicitly retain Rule-level limitation/authorization regarding public statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum procedure — delete assembly-initiated referendum
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to delete the section permitting an assembly-initiated referendum from Rule VII, because it has not been used and is unlikely to be utilized given the size and conduct of the membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain Board-initiated and member petition referendum procedures which are considered sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursements wording change — 'transmitting' vs 'filing'
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to make minor editorial changes to Rule VIII to reflect the practice of 'transmitting' the Bar's disbursement and financial information to the Court rather than 'filing' that information with the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use terminology that accurately reflects current practice and reduces confusion over procedural expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule IX wording change — 'promulgated' to 'established'
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to replace the word 'promulgated' with 'established' in Rule IX to indicate that the Rule relates to the vote required to create the original Bylaws after the creation of the D.C. Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose wording that better reflects the substantive meaning and historical context of the provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylaws amendment procedure to reside in Bylaws (delete Rule XV §2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that Rule XV, Section 2 be deleted because the provision governing Bylaw amendments exists appropriately in Bylaws Article X. Final approved Bylaws language: 'These Bylaws may be amended at any regular or special meeting of the Board by a two-thirds vote of the members of the Board of Governors present and voting, provided that notice of the amendment has been submitted in writing to the Board with the agenda of the meeting.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundancy between Rules and Bylaws and ensure amendment procedures are prescribed in the Bylaws consistent with Robert's Rules (advance notice and two-thirds vote).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership Manual as companion document with force and CEO discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3.01 establishes a District of Columbia Bar Membership Manual as a companion document to the Bylaws that has the full force and authority of the Bylaws, enabling a more streamlined process for amending operational/administrative membership procedures. Section 3.07 grants the CEO limited authority to make changes to a member's official record or require other action in the event of a Bar error or omission, or other good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a Membership Manual for operational details (subject to Executive Committee oversight); CEO discretion should be narrowly confined to rare, documented exceptions for hardship or administrative error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition changes — Treasurer-Elect and public member definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4.01 introduces the role of a Treasurer-Elect, redefines non-voting members as 'public members who are not members of the Bar,' and provides for appointment of a Secretary by the President from among elected members, subject to Board approval. Treasurer-Elect serves a three-year staggered sequence (Treasurer-Elect, Treasurer, then at-large voting member).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes are intended to balance electoral selection, attract qualified treasurers, preserve institutional knowledge, and provide continuity in financial oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board duties (expanded list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised Board duties (with new items noted) include: (a) To evaluate whether the needs of the organization’s members are being met; (b) To develop a long-range strategic plan and measure progress; (c) To request, receive, consider and take action on reports and recommendations; (d) To ensure accurate financial reporting, approve the annual budget, monitor financial condition, and review the outside audit; (e) To fix time/place of the annual meeting; (f) To arrange for publication of an official Bar bulletin or journal; (g) To conduct investigations of matters affecting the Bar; (h) To authorize, when appropriate, public statements on major issues of public interest or concern; (i) To adopt Bylaws and regulations not inconsistent with the Rules; and (j) To appoint, actively support, and work in partnership with the Chief Executive Officer, providing information and clear direction and evaluating the CEO’s performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these duty statements to guide Board governance, strategic planning, financial oversight, public communications, and CEO oversight; note that additions at (a), (b), (h), and (j) reflect best practices and clarifications of Board authority.
